label: late encoding-phase new tokens and the <DEL> step (end of input, before copying)
explanation: Fires only in the original/encoding phase and at the delimiter, never during copy (zero activations at t>L). 61% of mass is on the <DEL> step (45% of delimiters active), the rest on late original-phase steps (t>=5, rate rising with position: 9% at orig_idx 5 to 52% at orig_idx 8), almost always on the first occurrence of a token (in_first carries 93% of mass; repeated tokens rarely fire). Rate and magnitude grow with sequence length L and step t: top activations are at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences, with ramping activations on the preceding 3-4 tokens. Also modulated by the first original token (the token to be output next at <DEL>): w, k, q, 2, g are strongest, c and d weakest. Does not fire at t<=3 or anywhere in the copy phase. Predicate (phase<=1)&(t>=6)&(in_first==1) gets dev F1 0.59, mass recall 0.88; precision is limited (~0.47) because many qualifying steps stay inactive in a way partly but not fully explained by first-token identity and L.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, k, 2, g, q, l; least: 0, m, 1, h) and the current input token, by step (t=6: m, h, 1, j; t=5: m, h, 1, j; t=4: m, h, 1, z); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, L=9 & t=8, phase=1.
